title: Document-Level Event Factuality Identification Using Negation and Speculation Scope
abstract: Studies document-level event factuality identification using information about negation and speculation scope. It extends factuality assessment beyond isolated local cues, while remaining primarily a factuality component rather than a longitudinal state model.

admission.reason: The abstract shows document-level factuality classification using negation and speculation scope, but not source-relative holders, longitudinal revision, independent corroboration, or state transitions. It adds another isolated factuality component to a corpus whose open gaps concern combining such components over time.

title: Modality and Negation in Event Extraction
abstract: Presents an open-domain event extraction system that explicitly captures modality and negation so that possible, intended, or otherwise non-actual events are not automatically interpreted as having occurred. It supplies component semantics for distinguishing actual events from modal alternatives.

admission.reason: The paper explicitly captures modality and negation in event extraction, but the abstract does not show longitudinal tracking, scope changes across successive communications, correction, supersession, or evidence confirmation. It is useful component semantics but does not materially address the still-open longitudinal gaps beyond already established modality/factuality work.

title: TimeML: Robust Specification of Event and Temporal Expressions in Text
abstract: Defines a temporal annotation language that anchors event predicates to temporal expressions and orders events relative to one another both within sentences and across discourse. The representation also covers underspecified temporal expressions, aspectual predication, and modal subordination.
venue: New Directions in Question Answering, Papers from the 2003 AAAI Spring Symposium

admission.reason: TimeML is directly relevant temporal representation background, but the abstract describes event/time anchoring and temporal ordering rather than longitudinal work-item state, correction, supersession, provenance or evidence resolution. The current gaps explicitly arise from combining already validated component capabilities, so another general temporal annotation paper does not materially strengthen the unresolved streams this round.

title: Graph based Neural Networks for Event Factuality Prediction using Syntactic and Semantic Structures
abstract: Models event factuality using graph-based neural networks that combine syntactic and semantic sentence structures. The work addresses sentence-level assessment of whether an event is presented as having happened.

admission.reason: The abstract presents another sentence-level event factuality model based on syntactic and semantic graphs. It does not add source-relative holders, longitudinal transitions, evidential corroboration, or correction-sensitive state history, so its capability largely duplicates the isolated factuality component already represented in the programme.

title: The nature of requests and commitments in email messages
abstract: Studies task-oriented requests and commitments in workplace email and defines them at utterance level rather than only classifying whole messages. The work is motivated by tracking outstanding promises and unmet requests and reports annotation experiments on Enron email, providing workplace-specific component evidence even though it does not itself implement full longitudinal state tracking.

admission.reason: The workplace-email domain is highly relevant to gap-4, but the abstract explicitly describes utterance-level request and commitment identification rather than evaluating how the same work item changes state across successive messages. That capability belongs to Topic 05's already handed-off extraction boundary and does not demonstrate Topic 06 longitudinal lifecycle tracking.

title: Domain Knowledge Empowered Structured Neural Net for End-to-End Event Temporal Relation Extraction
abstract: Combines neural temporal-relation extraction with probabilistic domain constraints and structured inference. Lagrangian relaxation is used to incorporate distributional constraints rather than assuming that all structural knowledge is an infallible hard rule.

admission.reason: The paper provides structured temporal-relation extraction with probabilistic constraints, but it remains an isolated temporal component. The open gaps are not a lack of temporal classifiers; they concern longitudinal state revision, source-relative factuality, contradiction, provenance and their integration. The abstract does not show those capabilities.

title: He Thinks He Knows Better than the Doctors: BERT for Event Factuality Fails on Pragmatics
abstract: Evaluates BERT-based factuality prediction across multiple English datasets and shows that high aggregate performance can rely on surface regularities. The models remain unreliable on examples requiring pragmatic reasoning, illustrating limitations of static factuality classification.
venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics

admission.reason: The pragmatic failure analysis is useful evidence about limitations of static factuality predictors, but the abstract does not introduce a mechanism for longitudinal state tracking, source-relative corroboration, correction or provenance. It diagnoses an existing component rather than materially filling one of this round's state-evolution gaps.

title: Does It Happen? Multi-hop Path Structures for Event Factuality Prediction with Graph Transformer Networks
abstract: Introduces an event-factuality model that explicitly represents multi-hop syntactic and semantic paths between words rather than only direct graph connections. Experiments test whether richer sentence structure improves assessment of an event's factual degree.

admission.reason: The contribution is a richer graph architecture for event factuality prediction. The abstract does not demonstrate source-holder tracking, evidence corroboration, cross-message revision, or preservation of historical assessments, making it another isolated factuality model rather than a longitudinal-state contribution.

title: A Consensus Glossary of Temporal Database Concepts
abstract: Standardizes definitions for temporal-database concepts and explains distinctions among temporal notions used by the database community. It provides representation vocabulary relevant to valid time, transaction time, bitemporal information, and preservation of historical database states.

admission.reason: The glossary supplies useful terminology for valid time, transaction time and bitemporal data, but its abstract-level contribution is principally definitional. The candidate on resolution of time concepts more directly addresses event time, delayed updates, corrections and preservation of past states, so this paper would consume a reading slot without materially stronger capability. Identity is also UNCHECKED.

title: Joint Constrained Learning for Event-Event Relation Extraction
abstract: Jointly models temporal and subevent relations among event mentions and converts logical constraints across those relations into differentiable learning objectives. The resulting event complexes encode temporal ordering and event-membership structure with cross-relation consistency.

admission.reason: Joint temporal and subevent extraction with logical consistency is relevant temporal reasoning, but the abstract does not address evolving factual status, correction, supersession, contradiction between successive observations or provenance. It strengthens an already represented temporal component rather than one of the unresolved longitudinal combinations.

title: Global Inference to Chinese Temporal Relation Extraction
abstract: Introduces discourse-level global inference for temporal relations between event mentions, including relations spanning nonadjacent sentences. Semantic constraints are used to improve coherence of document-level temporal interpretation.

admission.reason: The paper performs discourse-level temporal relation extraction with global consistency, but the abstract does not model lifecycle states, changing factual assessments, provenance or correction semantics. Its core capability is already represented by stronger temporal-reasoning candidates and does not close the longitudinal gaps.

title: Beyond Pairwise: Global Zero-shot Temporal Graph Generation
abstract: Generates a document's complete temporal graph in a single zero-shot step and then applies temporal constraint optimization to enforce consistency among relations. It also introduces OmniTemp, with complete temporal annotations for targeted event pairs within documents.

admission.reason: Generating complete document temporal graphs with constraint optimization is a strong temporal-reasoning contribution, but the open problem is not simply incomplete temporal graphs. The abstract does not show state supersession, correction, source-relative factuality, evidential confirmation or immutable longitudinal history, so it remains an isolated F03 component rather than addressing the round's key missing integration.

title: Lexicosyntactic Inference in Neural Models
abstract: Uses event factuality prediction to study inferences created by interactions between lexical items and syntactic contexts. It introduces factuality judgments for English clause-embedding verbs across syntactic environments and exposes systematic errors in neural models.

admission.reason: The paper uses factuality judgments to probe lexical-syntactic inference and neural-model errors. It neither tracks a work item longitudinally nor represents sources, revisions, corroboration or state history. The capability therefore duplicates static factuality analysis rather than materially strengthening the target streams.

title: Toward Consistent and Informative Event-Event Temporal Relation Extraction
abstract: Constructs temporal event graphs while explicitly addressing global inconsistency, semantically irrelevant links, and lack of neighborhood context. The method combines pretrained language representations with graph neural modeling and constraints intended to produce globally consistent temporal orderings.

admission.reason: The abstract addresses consistency of temporal event graphs, but not consistency of changing lifecycle assessments or contradictions between successive communications. It adds another temporal-graph method without source-relative factuality, correction, provenance or revision semantics, so it does not materially address the remaining gaps.

title: Clinical Temporal Relation Extraction with Probabilistic Soft Logic Regularization and Global Inference
abstract: Performs document-level extraction of temporal relations among clinical events using probabilistic soft logic regularization and global inference. It explicitly models global relational dependencies rather than classifying event pairs independently.

admission.reason: The clinical system uses global inference for document-level temporal relations, but the abstract does not demonstrate longitudinal factual-state revision, supersession, conflicting updates or evidence lineage. Its transfer value is therefore redundant with the already represented temporal-relation stream and too distant from the unresolved workplace-state problem.

title: Neural Models of Factuality
abstract: Presents neural models for event factuality prediction and evaluates them on FactBank, UW, MEANTIME, and an expanded Universal Decompositional Semantics factuality dataset. It provides component evidence for determining whether textual events are presented as having occurred.

admission.reason: This is broad benchmark evidence for neural event factuality prediction, but the abstract concerns static textual factuality rather than longitudinal revision, multiple holders, independent corroboration or historical-state preservation. The corpus already has factuality as a validated component, so this does not materially close an open gap.
